entries.title: Asking about the database fleet in plain language
entries.summary: Gemini chat in Database Center answers fleet-health questions with project-specific recommendations.

entries.title: Seeing Bigtable and Memorystore in the database fleet view
entries.summary: Database Center covers Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Spanner, Bigtable, Firestore, Memorystore and more.

entries.title: Blocking new resources that are not CMEK-protected
entries.summary: The gcp.restrictNonCmekServices organization policy constraint requires CMEK for the listed services.

entries.title: CMEK for every team without creating keys by hand
entries.summary: Cloud KMS Autokey provisions keys on demand in a key project when developers create resources.

entries.title: A CMEK dataset in the EU that will not create
entries.summary: The Cloud KMS key's location must match the resource's location, for example eu for an EU multi-region dataset.

entries.title: Moving a VPC's firewall rules into a network firewall policy
entries.summary: The firewall-rules migrate command builds a global network firewall policy from existing VPC rules.

entries.title: Letting projects decide traffic an org policy should not judge
entries.summary: A hierarchical rule with action goto_next passes evaluation down to lower levels.

entries.title: Seeing which connections a policy rule is matching
entries.summary: Enable logging on the specific firewall policy rule to write Firewall Rules Logging entries.

entries.title: An on-call engineer who cannot see Service Health events
entries.summary: Grant roles/servicehealth.viewer (and enable the Service Health API) for least-privilege access.

entries.title: The Gemini Cloud Assist panel will not work in a new project
entries.summary: Enable the Gemini Cloud Assist API and grant users roles/geminicloudassist.user.

entries.title: Making sense of a latency spike on a dashboard chart
entries.summary: Gemini Cloud Assist can explain a metric chart or log entry in context and suggest next steps.

entries.title: Why an Autopilot HPA scales out too late
entries.summary: HPA CPU utilisation is measured against requests; oversized requests delay scaling and cost more.

entries.title: Several small inference Pods sharing one GPU
entries.summary: GPU time-sharing lets several containers share one physical GPU on a GKE node.

entries.title: Hard isolation between workloads on one A100
entries.summary: Multi-instance GPUs partition an A100/H100 into isolated instances with their own memory and compute.

entries.title: An identity that belongs to one agent only
entries.summary: Agent Identity gives each agent deployed to Agent Runtime its own principal, tied to the agent's lifecycle.

entries.title: Decommissioning an agent completely
entries.summary: Deleting an agent leaves its IAM bindings in place; remove them as part of decommissioning.

entries.title: BigQuery notebook runtimes on a private network
entries.summary: An administrator's runtime template fixes the network, subnet and public-IP setting for notebook runtimes.

entries.title: Collecting diagnostics from a misbehaving Workbench instance
entries.summary: gcloud workbench instances diagnose gathers logs and system data into a bucket for support.

entries.title: Workstations reachable only from the corporate network
entries.summary: A private workstation cluster uses a private gateway reached through Private Service Connect.

entries.title: A GPU in a data scientist's workstation
entries.summary: The workstation configuration specifies the GPU; Cloud Workstations attaches it and installs drivers.

entries.title: Protecting a database from a Cloud Run scale-out
entries.summary: Set maximum instances so a traffic burst cannot open more database connections than the database allows.

entries.title: A node pool upgrade that can be rolled back quickly
entries.summary: Blue-green node pool upgrades keep the old nodes during a soak period so you can roll back.

entries.title: A changed ConfigMap the Pods ignore
entries.summary: Environment variables from a ConfigMap are read at start; restart the Deployment to pick up changes.

entries.title: Scaling workers on a Pub/Sub backlog
entries.summary: An HPA on an external metric such as a subscription's undelivered messages scales queue consumers.

entries.title: Docker Hub rate limits breaking deployments
entries.summary: An Artifact Registry remote repository caches Docker Hub images inside Google Cloud.

entries.title: Snapshots that must stay in Germany
entries.summary: Choose the snapshot storage location (region or multi-region) explicitly to meet residency rules.

entries.title: Every Pending Pod across all namespaces
entries.summary: Use kubectl get pods -A with a field selector on status.phase.

entries.title: Moving old objects onto the new key version
entries.summary: Rotation does not re-encrypt existing data; rewrite objects so they use the new primary version.

entries.title: Undoing a key destruction request
entries.summary: Destroyed key versions stay in 'scheduled for destruction' (30 days by default) and can be restored meanwhile.

entries.title: Backups that ransomware and rogue admins cannot delete
entries.summary: Backup and DR Service backup vaults enforce a minimum retention that nobody can shorten.

entries.title: Reading Spanner data as it was an hour ago
entries.summary: Spanner point-in-time recovery uses version_retention_period (up to 7 days) for stale reads and restores.

entries.title: Joining Cloud SQL rows with BigQuery tables in one query
entries.summary: BigQuery federated queries use EXTERNAL_QUERY through a Cloud SQL connection.

entries.title: Paying for compressed bytes in BigQuery storage
entries.summary: Switching a dataset to the physical storage billing model bills compressed bytes, often far cheaper.

entries.title: Getting back an object deleted three days ago
entries.summary: Soft delete keeps deleted objects for a retention window (7 days by default), even without versioning.

entries.title: Sending only one subnet's traffic through an inspection appliance
entries.summary: A policy-based route matches source/destination/protocol and sends matching traffic to an internal LB.

entries.title: A highly available next hop for a static route
entries.summary: Use an internal passthrough Network Load Balancer as next hop to spread across healthy appliances.

entries.title: A peered VPC that cannot see the VPN routes
entries.summary: Export custom routes on one side and import them on the other for peered VPCs to use them.

entries.title: A GKE cluster that has run out of Pod addresses
entries.summary: Add an additional (discontiguous) Pod IPv4 range and use it for new node pools.

entries.title: One address for a global load balancer that must never change
entries.summary: Reserve a global static external IP address and use it in the global forwarding rule.

entries.title: Every firewall rule that actually applies to one VM
entries.summary: get-effective-firewalls shows hierarchical, network-policy and VPC rules applying to an interface.

entries.title: NAT port exhaustion on a few busy VMs
entries.summary: Dynamic port allocation lets busy VMs get more NAT ports while quiet VMs keep few.

entries.title: A cryptic log entry during an incident
entries.summary: Logs Explorer can ask Gemini Cloud Assist to explain a log entry in plain language.

entries.title: Which application's deployment failed last night
entries.summary: Cloud Hub's deployments view shows recent GKE and Cloud Run deployments, including failed App Hub ones.

entries.title: Cost of one application across its projects
entries.summary: Cloud Hub's Optimization page shows cost and utilisation per project or App Hub application.

entries.title: Paging on how fast the error budget is burning
entries.summary: An SLO burn-rate alert pages when the error budget is being consumed too quickly.

entries.title: Testing a multi-step checkout journey every five minutes
entries.summary: Synthetic monitors run scripted tests (such as browser flows) on a schedule and alert on failure.

entries.title: An uptime check for a service with no public address
entries.summary: Private uptime checks reach internal endpoints through Service Directory.

entries.title: Existing Grafana dashboards on Managed Service for Prometheus
entries.summary: Grafana queries Managed Service for Prometheus with PromQL through a Cloud Monitoring data source.

entries.title: OpenTelemetry-instrumented services on Google Cloud
entries.summary: Send OpenTelemetry metrics and traces to Cloud Monitoring and Cloud Trace through an OpenTelemetry Collector.

entries.title: VPC Flow Logs costing more than they are worth
entries.summary: Lower the sampling rate and lengthen the aggregation interval to reduce flow log volume.

entries.title: What TERMINATED means in the instance list
entries.summary: TERMINATED means stopped, not deleted: the VM still exists and its disks and reserved addresses still cost money.

entries.title: Every VM in the organization, not one project
entries.summary: gcloud compute instances list is scoped to one project; Cloud Asset Inventory searches across an organization.

entries.title: Applying a lifecycle configuration from a file
entries.summary: A lifecycle configuration is a bucket-level JSON document, applied with gcloud storage buckets update --lifecycle-file.

entries.title: A live-only age rule that never frees versioned storage
entries.summary: With Object Versioning on, a Delete rule limited to isLive true only makes live objects noncurrent; removing those versions needs a rule that can match them.

entries.title: Deleting Coldline objects after a month
entries.summary: Each colder class has a minimum storage duration; deleting early is charged as if the object stayed the full minimum.

entries.title: New revisions that never receive traffic
entries.summary: Once traffic is pinned to a named revision, new deployments get no traffic until it is sent to the latest revision again.

entries.title: Changing an environment variable on Cloud Run
entries.summary: Any configuration change to a Cloud Run service, such as an environment variable, creates a new revision.

entries.title: Clearing out abandoned multipart uploads
entries.summary: The AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload lifecycle action removes multipart uploads left unfinished for a set number of days.

entries.title: A lifecycle rule that has not acted yet
entries.summary: Lifecycle actions are asynchronous; after you add or change a rule, it can take up to 24 hours to take effect.

entries.title: Pausing a VM with its memory kept
entries.summary: Suspending a VM saves its memory to storage and lets it resume where it left off; stopping discards memory.

entries.title: Giving a running VM more vCPUs
entries.summary: A VM's machine type can be changed only while it is stopped.

entries.title: A BigQuery job that cannot be found
entries.summary: BigQuery jobs are tied to a location; looking one up needs the job's location as well as its ID.

entries.title: A CI gate on bytes scanned
entries.summary: A BigQuery dry run reports the bytes a query would process without running it, which a CI check can compare with a limit.

entries.title: Tables nobody modifies any more
entries.summary: BigQuery bills tables or partitions unmodified for 90 consecutive days at the lower long-term storage price, automatically.

entries.title: One switch for object-level permissions
entries.summary: Uniform bucket-level access disables ACLs so that access to every object is controlled by IAM alone.

entries.title: A one-hour download link for an outsider
entries.summary: A signed URL grants time-limited access to one object to anyone who has the link, with no Google account needed.

entries.title: Sharing a custom image with another project
entries.summary: Granting Compute Image User on an image, or its project, lets principals elsewhere create VMs from it.

entries.title: Credentials for a new Windows VM
entries.summary: gcloud compute reset-windows-password creates or resets a local Windows account and returns its password.

entries.title: A CPU-heavy service drowning in parallel requests
entries.summary: Lowering concurrency on a CPU-bound Cloud Run service makes it add instances instead of overloading each one.

entries.title: Querying CSV files where they already are
entries.summary: A BigQuery external table queries files in Cloud Storage in place, without loading them.

entries.title: Configuration-change records for three years
entries.summary: Admin Activity logs stay 400 days in the _Required bucket; longer retention needs a sink to a destination you control.

entries.title: Settings and a password for the same Pods
entries.summary: Keep non-sensitive configuration in a ConfigMap and credentials in a Secret, both outside the image, and reference them from the Pod spec.

entries.title: No cold starts, and a cap on Cloud Run cost
entries.summary: Minimum instances keep instances warm to avoid cold starts; maximum instances cap how far the service scales out.

entries.title: Upgrading nodes without dropping below two replicas
entries.summary: Surge upgrades with maxUnavailable 0 add a new node before draining an old one, and a PodDisruptionBudget stops drains from evicting too many replicas at once.

entries.title: A Cloud SQL database that survives a region outage
entries.summary: For regional disaster recovery on Cloud SQL, keep a cross-region read replica to promote, and store backups in a location outside the primary region.

entries.title: Proving which firewall rule allowed a connection
entries.summary: Firewall Rules Logging records each connection a rule allows or denies, and the entries are read in Cloud Logging.

entries.title: Apache logs and metrics from a VM fleet
entries.summary: The Ops Agent collects system metrics and logs, and its configuration file adds receivers for third-party applications such as Apache.

entries.title: Logs for analysis now and a cheap archive for years
entries.summary: Use one sink to BigQuery for SQL analysis and another to a Cloud Storage bucket for long, low-cost retention.

entries.title: Signing in to a new Windows VM through IAP
entries.summary: A Windows VM needs a generated Windows password, and with IAP TCP forwarding, port 3389 opened to IAP's range.

entries.title: Knowing a query's cost before running it
entries.summary: A dry run, or the console's query validator, reports the bytes a query would process without running it; on-demand cost follows from those bytes.

entries.title: A vendor's allow-list and a NAT address that changed
entries.summary: Automatic NAT IP allocation can add or change addresses; manual assignment of reserved static IPs keeps egress on fixed addresses.

entries.title: Cloud NAT that works in one region only
entries.summary: Cloud NAT is regional: each region with private VMs that need internet egress needs its own Cloud Router and NAT gateway.

entries.title: Keeping a load balancer's current address before a rebuild
entries.summary: An in-use ephemeral external address can be promoted to a static address, so a rebuilt load balancer can keep the exact IP customers already allow-list.

entries.title: A VM whose public address changed after a restart
entries.summary: A VM needs a reserved regional static external address to keep its public IP through stops and replacement; global addresses are for global load balancers.

entries.title: Where on-premises DNS sends queries for a private zone
entries.summary: An inbound server policy allocates entry-point addresses in the VPC's subnets; on-premises resolvers forward the private zone's domain to them.

entries.title: A forwarding zone whose answers never arrive
entries.summary: Cloud DNS sends forwarded queries from 35.199.192.0/19 over the hybrid connection, so on-premises firewalls and routes must allow that range.

entries.title: An Autopilot cluster that ran out of Pod addresses
entries.summary: Autopilot clusters on GKE 1.26 and later can take additional Pod IPv4 ranges from new subnet secondary ranges, used for nodes in new node pools.

entries.title: How many secondary ranges one subnet can hold
entries.summary: A subnet can have up to 170 secondary IPv4 ranges, a limit that can't be raised; ranges must not overlap anything else in the VPC.

entries.title: Using a workstation someone else created
entries.summary: The Cloud Workstations User role on a workstation lets a person start and use it; creating workstations needs the Creator role on a configuration.

entries.title: Counting errors from a log field
entries.summary: A counter log-based metric counts matching log entries, which is how an error rate is charted and alerted on; distribution metrics are for numeric values such as latency.

entries.title: Latency hidden in a plain-text log line
entries.summary: A distribution log-based metric can extract a number from textPayload with a regular expression, and percentiles are charted from the resulting histogram.

entries.title: A sink into another project's bucket that writes nothing
entries.summary: A sink writes as its writer identity, which needs a role on the destination: for a Cloud Storage bucket, Storage Object Creator.

entries.title: A PodMonitoring resource in the wrong namespace
entries.summary: PodMonitoring is namespaced and selects Pods only in its own namespace; ClusterPodMonitoring selects across namespaces.

entries.title: Health metrics for self-managed MySQL on VMs
entries.summary: The Ops Agent's MySQL integration collects MySQL metrics and logs from Compute Engine VMs into Cloud Monitoring and Cloud Logging, using generally available features.

entries.title: Serial console refused by policy
entries.summary: The interactive serial console needs serial-port-enable on the VM or project, and the compute.disableSerialPortAccess organisation policy must not be enforced on it.

entries.title: Reading why a VM doesn't finish booting
entries.summary: Serial port output shows a VM's boot and kernel messages without signing in, which is the first look at a VM that won't boot.

entries.title: A bigger machine type for every VM in a group
entries.summary: A managed instance group's machine type comes from its instance template; changing it means a new template and a rolling update, not editing each VM.

entries.title: A public address lost while resizing a VM
entries.summary: Changing a VM's machine type requires stopping it, and stopping releases an ephemeral external IP; promote it to static first to keep it.

entries.title: Testing a new setting on Cloud Run without users
entries.summary: Deploying with --no-traffic and a tag creates a revision that gets its own URL but no user traffic, for testing before a switch.

entries.title: Rolling back a bad configuration on Cloud Run
entries.summary: Each configuration change is a new immutable revision, so a rollback sends traffic back to the previous revision rather than editing the bad one.

entries.title: An inherited role that one project must not have
entries.summary: A child resource cannot remove an allow binding inherited from a parent; change the grant at its source.

entries.title: A Google-managed service agent needs access in another project
entries.summary: Service agents are Google-managed service accounts; when a service reads another project's resource, grant the agent.

entries.title: Deploying a service that runs as a service account
entries.summary: Attaching a service account to a resource requires iam.serviceAccounts.actAs — Service Account User on that account.

entries.title: One Cloud Run service calling another private service
entries.summary: The calling service's attached service account gets a short-lived ID token from the metadata server.

entries.title: Only one repository's pipeline may use the federation
entries.summary: An attribute condition on the workload identity provider restricts which external tokens are accepted.

entries.title: A custom role needed in forty projects
entries.summary: A custom role created in a project can be granted only in that project; create it at the organisation to reuse it.

entries.title: Every binding that applies to a project, including inherited ones
entries.summary: gcloud projects get-ancestors-iam-policy shows the policies of the project and all its ancestors.

entries.title: Granting a Kubernetes service account access directly
entries.summary: Workload Identity Federation for GKE lets you bind IAM roles directly to a Kubernetes service account principal.

entries.title: A least-privilege identity for GKE nodes
entries.summary: Give GKE nodes a minimal custom service account instead of the Editor-bearing default compute account.

entries.title: Retiring a service account you think is unused
entries.summary: Disable a service account first: it is reversible, unlike deletion, and shows whether anything still depends on it.

entries.title: Stop new default service accounts receiving Editor
entries.summary: The iam.automaticIamGrantsForDefaultServiceAccounts constraint stops default service accounts getting Editor.

entries.title: Who is allowed to impersonate a service account
entries.summary: Access to a service account is set on the service account itself as a resource; read its own IAM policy.

entries.title: Running every gcloud command as a service account
entries.summary: gcloud config set auth/impersonate_service_account makes all commands impersonate one service account.

entries.title: Using a federated identity from application code
entries.summary: A WIF credential configuration file tells client libraries how to exchange the external token; it holds no secret.

entries.title: Two scripts editing the same policy at once
entries.summary: set-iam-policy uses the policy's etag, so a concurrent change makes the second write fail instead of overwriting it.

entries.title: Production admin rights only during an incident
entries.summary: Privileged Access Manager grants time-bound, approved, audited elevation on request.

entries.title: A role that applies only to resources tagged env=dev
entries.summary: An IAM condition with resource.matchTag limits a grant to resources carrying a tag value.

entries.title: Network builders who must not touch firewalls
entries.summary: compute.networkAdmin manages networks, subnets and routes but not firewall rules; compute.securityAdmin does firewalls.

entries.title: Calling an IAP-protected app from a script
entries.summary: An OIDC ID token for a service account, minted with the correct audience, authenticates to IAP or Cloud Run.

entries.title: Signed URLs with no key file
entries.summary: A signed URL can be signed through impersonation (signBlob), with no service-account key.

entries.title: An access token that must last eight hours
entries.summary: Access tokens last one hour by default; up to 12 hours needs the credential-lifetime organisation policy.

entries.title: A JWT for a partner API, signed without a key
entries.summary: The IAM Credentials signJwt method signs a JWT with a service account's Google-managed key.

entries.title: A host-network Pod that ignores Workload Identity
entries.summary: Pods that use the host network cannot use Workload Identity Federation for GKE; they see the node's identity.

entries.title: Linking a Kubernetes service account to an IAM service account
entries.summary: Grant roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser to PROJECT.svc.id.goog[NS/KSA] on the IAM SA and annotate the KSA.

entries.title: The same Pod works in one namespace but not another
entries.summary: A Workload Identity principal names the namespace and KSA, so a copy in another namespace is a different principal.

entries.title: Custom node account pulling from another project
entries.summary: A custom node service account needs Artifact Registry Reader on a repository in another project to pull from it.

entries.title: An AWS workload reading from Google Cloud
entries.summary: An AWS provider in a workload identity pool accepts AWS roles, exchanged for short-lived Google tokens.

entries.title: An Azure workload calling Google Cloud
entries.summary: Workloads on Azure federate through an OIDC provider that trusts the Entra ID tenant's issuer.

entries.title: Who may create pools and providers
entries.summary: Workload Identity Pool Admin manages pools and providers; it is separate from using them.

entries.title: On-premises servers with certificates but no IdP
entries.summary: Workload Identity Federation can trust X.509 certificates issued by your own CA.

entries.title: Granting a key role to a service agent that does not exist yet
entries.summary: Force-create a service agent with gcloud beta services identity create before its first use.

entries.title: Restoring a service account deleted last week
entries.summary: A deleted service account can be undeleted within 30 days using its unique ID, keeping its bindings.

entries.title: Renaming a service account
entries.summary: A service account's email (its ID) is permanent; only the display name and description can change.

entries.title: Who acted through a service account
entries.summary: Audit log entries for impersonated calls record the original caller in serviceAccountDelegationInfo.

entries.title: A build trigger that runs as a chosen service account
entries.summary: Choosing a service account for a Cloud Build trigger requires actAs (Service Account User) on it.

entries.title: ID tokens only, not access tokens
entries.summary: roles/iam.serviceAccountOpenIdTokenCreator lets a caller mint OIDC ID tokens but not OAuth access tokens.

entries.title: Managing one service account, not all of them
entries.summary: Roles granted on a single service account resource apply to that account only.

entries.title: Attaching a service account from another project
entries.summary: Attaching a service account from a different project needs actAs and the cross-project usage constraint not enforced.

entries.title: A VM denied despite the right IAM role
entries.summary: Legacy access scopes limit what a VM's service account can do, on top of IAM.

entries.title: Consuming from one subscription only
entries.summary: Grant Pub/Sub Subscriber on the single subscription rather than on the project.

entries.title: A federated pipeline that must act as a service account
entries.summary: Grant roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser on the service account to the federated principal set, then impersonate.

entries.title: Federating a Kubernetes cluster whose issuer is private
entries.summary: Upload the cluster's JWKS to the OIDC provider (--jwk-json-path) when Google cannot fetch the issuer's keys.

entries.title: Keeping a team's identities inside its own projects
entries.summary: Principal access boundary policies limit which resources principals are eligible to access, whatever they are granted.

entries.title: Access only during business hours
entries.summary: An IAM condition on request.time limits when a role binding is effective.

entries.title: Letting a team grant only a few roles
entries.summary: A condition on setIamPolicy using modifiedGrantsByRole limits which roles a delegate may grant.

entries.title: Access to every bucket whose name starts with logs-
entries.summary: An IAM condition on resource.name.startsWith scopes a project-level grant to matching buckets.

entries.title: Reviewing IAM policies across the organisation without data access
entries.summary: Security Reviewer grants permission to list and get IAM policies on all resources, not to read data.

entries.title: An IAM policy that has grown too large
entries.summary: Allow policies have a principal limit (1,500); consolidate individual users into groups.

entries.title: Keeping production and staging pipelines apart
entries.summary: Separate workload identity pools per environment keep federated identities from crossing environments.

entries.title: Stopping an external workload's federation during an incident
entries.summary: Disable the workload identity provider (or pool) to stop new token exchanges immediately.

entries.title: Seeing which external workload made a call
entries.summary: Audit logs record federated principals (and delegation) so external workloads are attributable.

entries.title: Keys that expire on their own
entries.summary: The organisation policy iam.serviceAccountKeyExpiryHours limits the lifetime of new keys.

entries.title: An S3-compatible tool that needs Cloud Storage access
entries.summary: Cloud Storage HMAC keys for a service account let S3-compatible tools use the XML API.

entries.title: Cloud Scheduler calling a private Cloud Run service
entries.summary: Cloud Scheduler sends an OIDC token for a service account that has Cloud Run Invoker.

entries.title: Workload Identity Federation on Autopilot
entries.summary: Autopilot clusters have Workload Identity Federation for GKE enabled by default.

entries.title: GitHub Actions cannot get a token for federation
entries.summary: The workflow job needs permissions id-token: write so GitHub issues the OIDC token to exchange.

entries.title: Read-only access to Cloud Run and nothing else
entries.summary: A product's predefined viewer role grants read-only access to that product only, unlike the basic Viewer role.

entries.title: One service account per workload
entries.summary: Give each workload its own user-managed service account with only the roles it needs, and attach it instead of the Compute Engine default service account.

entries.title: A service account key pushed to a public repository
entries.summary: When a key leaks, disable or delete that key at once, then check audit logs for actions made with its key ID.

entries.title: A Cloud Run service that reads a secret and publishes events
entries.summary: Grant the service's own service account a narrow role on each resource it uses: Secret Accessor on the secret and Publisher on the topic.

entries.title: An external auditor who reads policies and audit logs
entries.summary: Security Reviewer reads IAM policies across resources, and Private Logs Viewer reads all logs including Data Access audit logs; neither can change anything.

entries.title: A service account deleted six weeks ago
entries.summary: A deleted service account can be undeleted only within 30 days; after that, create a new one and grant its roles again.

entries.title: A recreated service account that still gets permission denied
entries.summary: Role bindings point at a service account's unique ID, so a new account with the same email doesn't inherit the deleted account's bindings.

entries.title: Which keys authenticated this month
entries.summary: Cloud Monitoring's service account key metrics record authentication events per key for six weeks, which shows which keys are still in use.

entries.title: An HMAC key that belongs to a person
entries.summary: HMAC keys for interoperability should belong to a service account with a role on the specific bucket, not to a user account.

entries.title: Which endpoint an S3 tool must call
entries.summary: S3-compatible tools use Cloud Storage's XML API at https://storage.googleapis.com with an HMAC key.

entries.title: A scheduled call to Cloud Run that returns 403
entries.summary: Cloud Run accepts Google-signed ID tokens; a Cloud Scheduler job must send an OIDC token, not an OAuth access token, for a service account with Invoker.

entries.title: A scheduled job that calls a Google API
entries.summary: Cloud Scheduler sends OAuth access tokens to Google APIs on *.googleapis.com, and OIDC tokens to your own endpoints such as Cloud Run.

entries.title: Testing a policy change, explaining a denial
entries.summary: Policy Simulator shows the effect of an allow policy change before it is made; Policy Troubleshooter explains one principal's access to one resource.

entries.title: Everyone who can read one sensitive dataset
entries.summary: Policy Analyzer answers which principals have what access to a resource, across inherited policies and groups.

entries.title: Developers locked out after the project moved folders
entries.summary: When a project moves, policies inherited from its old parent stop applying, while policies attached to the project itself stay.

entries.title: Read access for every employee, present and future
entries.summary: A domain principal stands for all Google Accounts in the Cloud Identity or Workspace domain, so new accounts are covered automatically.

entries.title: Access that did not expire with its condition
entries.summary: A conditional binding does not limit a principal who also holds the same role without a condition; the unconditional binding must go.

entries.title: An operator for a single VM
entries.summary: Some resources, such as a Compute Engine instance, accept their own allow policy, so a role can be limited to one resource in a project.

entries.title: Read everywhere in the folder, edit in one project
entries.summary: The effective policy is the union of a resource's own policy and what it inherits, so a narrow folder grant plus a broader project grant adds up.

entries.title: Federated staff refused by allAuthenticatedUsers
entries.summary: allAuthenticatedUsers covers Google Accounts only, not federated identities; workforce pool users are granted access through the pool's principal set.

entries.title: The service agent is missing from the IAM page
entries.summary: The console's IAM page hides service agents until Include Google-provided role grants is selected.

entries.title: A project Owner cannot create a deny policy
entries.summary: Creating and managing deny policies requires the Deny Admin role; project ownership does not include it.

entries.title: A role on the IAM page that cannot be edited
entries.summary: An inherited role is shown on a child's IAM page but can be changed only on the resource where it was granted.

entries.title: An Owner who cannot delete a service account key
entries.summary: A deny policy on a resource or an ancestor is checked before allow policies, so it blocks a permission whatever roles the principal holds.

entries.title: A custom role deleted two days ago
entries.summary: A deleted custom role can be undeleted within 7 days; its bindings stay in the policies and take effect again.

entries.title: A GKE Pod reading one bucket without keys
entries.summary: Workload Identity Federation for GKE: grant the role to the Kubernetes ServiceAccount's principal on the resource, and run the Pod as that ServiceAccount.

entries.title: Two years of audit logs for the whole organization
entries.summary: An aggregated sink at the organization with children included routes every project's audit logs; the sink's writer identity needs write access on the destination.

entries.title: Cloud Run reachable only through the load balancer
entries.summary: Put Cloud Run behind an external Application Load Balancer with a serverless NEG, and set the service's ingress to internal and Cloud Load Balancing so the run.app URL stops accepting internet traffic.

entries.title: Stopping a sandbox's charges when its budget runs out
entries.summary: Budgets only notify. To stop charges, publish budget notifications to Pub/Sub and have a function disable billing on the project.

entries.title: Private GKE nodes that can't pull from Docker Hub
entries.summary: Private Google Access covers Google APIs such as Artifact Registry; reaching an internet registry from nodes without external IPs needs Cloud NAT.

entries.title: Terraform from GitHub Actions without a key
entries.summary: A workload identity pool with a GitHub OIDC provider, limited by an attribute condition, lets the repository's workflow impersonate the deploy service account with short-lived tokens.

entries.title: Undoing an accidental DELETE on Cloud SQL
entries.summary: Point-in-time recovery clones a Cloud SQL instance to a moment before the mistake, without losing the changes made since the last backup.

entries.title: No public buckets, but partners still get access
entries.summary: Public access prevention blocks allUsers and allAuthenticatedUsers on every bucket; uniform bucket-level access turns ACLs off; neither blocks named external accounts.

entries.title: One set of alerts for fifteen projects
entries.summary: A scoping project's metrics scope can include other projects, so alert policies and dashboards defined once there see all their metrics.

entries.title: Recreating VMs whose application hangs
entries.summary: MIG autohealing needs a health check on the group and a firewall rule that admits Google's health-check probe ranges.

entries.title: VM admin rights in every development project
entries.summary: A role granted on a folder is inherited by every project in it, including projects created there later, and by nothing outside it.

entries.title: Seven years kept, cheap after ninety days
entries.summary: A locked retention policy stops anyone deleting objects early; lifecycle rules change the storage class and delete objects by age without scripts.

entries.title: HA VPN that qualifies for the 99.99% SLA
entries.summary: HA VPN reaches its 99.99% SLA only with two tunnels from both gateway interfaces and dynamic (BGP) routing through Cloud Router.

entries.title: Creating VMs that run as an app service account
entries.summary: Creating a VM that runs as a service account needs a role to create instances and Service Account User on that service account.

entries.title: Autoscaling stopped by a regional CPU quota
entries.summary: A managed instance group that can't add VMs because of a regional quota needs a higher quota in that region, requested through Cloud Quotas.

entries.title: Knowing who reads a sensitive bucket from now on
entries.summary: Reads of Cloud Storage objects are recorded only in Data Access audit logs, which are off by default for Cloud Storage and are enabled in the IAM audit configuration.

entries.title: The cheapest VMs for restartable render jobs
entries.summary: Spot VMs are the cheapest Compute Engine capacity for fault-tolerant work that can be stopped at any time; commitments suit steady usage over one or three years.

entries.title: GPU jobs on GPU nodes only
entries.summary: Add a GPU node pool and request nvidia.com/gpu in the Pod's resource limits; GKE taints GPU nodes so that other Pods stay off them.

entries.title: A BigQuery dataset encrypted with the security team's key
entries.summary: For CMEK in BigQuery, the BigQuery service agent needs Encrypter/Decrypter on a key in the dataset's location, and the dataset's default key is set to it.

entries.title: Switching between two projects' gcloud settings
entries.summary: Named gcloud configurations hold a project, account and default region or zone each, and you activate one to switch them all at once.

entries.title: Only the web tier may receive load balancer traffic
entries.subtopic: Secure Tags and Service Accounts in Rules
entries.summary: A firewall rule can target VMs by the service account they run as, which only people allowed to act as that account can change.

entries.title: Product images that survive a region outage within minutes
entries.summary: A dual-region Cloud Storage bucket with turbo replication replicates new objects to both regions within 15 minutes (RPO), in the two regions you choose.

entries.title: SSH to private VMs through IAP
entries.summary: IAP TCP forwarding needs ingress from 35.235.240.0/20 on port 22 and the IAP-secured Tunnel User role for the people connecting.

entries.title: Contractors signing in with their own company's Okta
entries.summary: Workforce Identity Federation lets users from an external identity provider use the console with IAM roles granted to pool principals, without Cloud Identity accounts.

entries.title: Logs only the security team may read
entries.summary: Route sensitive logs to their own log bucket, keep them out of _Default, and grant access through a log view on that bucket.

entries.title: Paying per Pod with no nodes to manage
entries.summary: GKE Autopilot manages nodes and bills for the Pods' resource requests, so the team sets requests and nothing else.

entries.title: Trimming a service account that has too much access
entries.summary: IAM role recommendations compare granted permissions with the ones used over the last 90 days and suggest a smaller role.

entries.title: Orders kept while the consumer is down for hours
entries.summary: Pub/Sub decouples producers and consumers and retains unacknowledged messages in a subscription for up to seven days by default.

entries.title: One hour of access for someone without a Google account
entries.summary: A V4 signed URL grants time-limited access to one object to anyone holding the URL, signed by a service account the requester can use.

entries.title: Cost per team across shared projects
entries.summary: Labels on resources travel into the Cloud Billing export, so costs can be grouped by team in BigQuery even when teams share projects.

entries.title: Which function burns the CPU in production
entries.summary: Cloud Profiler samples CPU and memory use per function in production with low overhead; Trace shows latency between services.

entries.title: Processing each upload as it arrives
entries.summary: An Eventarc trigger on Cloud Storage's object-finalized event delivers each new object to a Cloud Run service, with no polling.

entries.title: A subnet that has run out of addresses
entries.summary: A subnet's primary range can be expanded in place, without downtime, as long as the new range doesn't overlap others; it can't be shrunk.

entries.title: Keeping BigQuery query costs in check
entries.summary: Partitioning with a filter on the partition column cuts bytes scanned; custom query quotas cap the bytes a user or project can process per day.

entries.title: Deploying an image from another project's registry
entries.summary: Cloud Run pulls images as its service agent, so a repository in another project must grant that project's Cloud Run service agent Artifact Registry Reader.

entries.title: Access that follows people as they join and leave
entries.summary: Grant IAM roles to Google groups managed in Cloud Identity, so that joining or leaving the group changes access without editing IAM policies.

entries.title: UDP game traffic that must keep client addresses
entries.summary: An external passthrough Network Load Balancer handles UDP and preserves client source IPs, so backend firewall rules must admit the clients' addresses.

entries.title: Daily disk backups kept for two weeks
entries.summary: A snapshot schedule attached to persistent disks takes snapshots automatically and deletes them after the retention you set.

entries.title: No external IPs except on the bastion
entries.summary: The compute.vmExternalIpAccess list constraint allows external IPs only on the VM instances you list.

entries.title: Only the break-glass group may delete projects
entries.summary: An IAM deny policy at the organization can deny a permission to everyone, with exception principals, and it overrides any allow policy below it.

entries.title: Pods and nodes both scaling for a traffic spike
entries.summary: On GKE Standard, the HorizontalPodAutoscaler adds Pods and the cluster autoscaler adds nodes when Pods can't be scheduled; both are needed for a spike.

entries.title: Running gcloud as the deploy service account
entries.summary: Service account impersonation needs Service Account Token Creator on that account; gcloud then uses short-lived tokens with --impersonate-service-account.

entries.title: Alerting on a burst of error logs
entries.summary: A counter log-based metric counts matching log entries, and an alerting policy on that metric fires when the count over a window crosses a threshold.

entries.title: An API used only in office hours
entries.summary: Cloud Run runs stateless containers, scales to zero when idle and bills for the time requests are processed by default.

entries.title: Partners who may upload but not read
entries.summary: Storage Object Creator allows creating objects without viewing, listing or overwriting them.

entries.title: Separating production from everything else
entries.summary: Folders group projects so that IAM grants and organization policies set once on a folder apply to all its projects.

entries.title: Proving which rule blocks traffic before sending any
entries.summary: Connectivity Tests analyse the configured path between two endpoints and name the firewall rule or route that blocks it, without sending traffic.

entries.title: An app on AWS reading Cloud Storage without keys
entries.summary: A workload identity pool with an AWS provider exchanges the EC2 instance's AWS credentials for short-lived Google tokens, so no service account key is needed.

entries.title: Two teams' VPCs talking over private addresses
entries.summary: VPC Network Peering connects two VPCs over internal IPs while each team keeps its own administration; firewall rules in each VPC still decide what's allowed.

entries.title: Notebook instances left running overnight
entries.summary: Vertex AI Workbench instances can shut down automatically after a set idle time, which stops compute charges while nobody uses them.

entries.title: An Eventarc trigger for new uploads that fails to create
entries.summary: Eventarc triggers for Cloud Storage events need the project's Cloud Storage service agent to hold Pub/Sub Publisher, because Cloud Storage publishes the events through Pub/Sub.

entries.title: GKE Pods reaching a private Cloud SQL instance without keys
entries.summary: Run the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy beside the app and give the Kubernetes ServiceAccount's principal Cloud SQL Client through Workload Identity Federation for GKE: IAM-authorized connections, no keys.

entries.title: A Cloud SQL database that must survive a region outage
entries.summary: Cloud SQL HA protects against a zone failure only. For a region failure with a small RPO, add a cross-region read replica and promote it.

entries.title: A rotated password that Cloud Run picks up without a redeploy
entries.summary: A secret mounted as a volume that references the latest version is read when the file is read, so new versions are picked up without a deploy; the runtime service account needs Secret Accessor on that secret.

entries.title: On-premises servers reaching only VPC-SC supported APIs
entries.summary: For on-premises access to Google APIs over Interconnect or VPN, advertise the VIP range from Cloud Router and point DNS at it; restricted.googleapis.com (199.36.153.4/30) reaches only APIs supported by VPC Service Controls.

entries.title: Cloud Run reaching a private Memorystore instance cheaply
entries.summary: Direct VPC egress gives a Cloud Run service an address in a VPC subnet with no connector instances to run or pay for.

entries.title: Logging charges driven by debug entries
entries.summary: Logging charges by volume ingested. An exclusion filter on the _Default sink drops unwanted entries before ingestion, while audit logs and other entries keep flowing.

entries.title: Rolling a new image without losing capacity
entries.summary: A proactive rolling update with max unavailable 0 adds new VMs before removing old ones; a regional MIG needs max surge of at least the number of zones.

entries.title: A single VM that must be rebuilt in another region
entries.summary: A snapshot schedule with a multi-region storage location gives daily, automatic restore points that survive a regional outage.

entries.title: Analysts querying another project's dataset
entries.summary: To query data in another project and bill the query to their own, users need BigQuery Data Viewer on the dataset and BigQuery Job User on the project that runs the job.

entries.title: Right-sizing underused VMs with little analysis
entries.summary: Recommender's machine type recommendations are based on observed utilization, so they are the low-effort, low-risk way to right-size VMs.

entries.title: No GKE upgrades during a sales freeze
entries.summary: A maintenance exclusion with the scope 'no minor or node upgrades' blocks minor and node upgrades for the period while still allowing control plane patches.

entries.title: Monitoring an internal service from outside its VMs
entries.summary: Private uptime checks reach internal endpoints registered in Service Directory; the VPC must allow ingress from the uptime checkers' range.

entries.title: An internal web app for one group, without a VPN
entries.summary: Identity-Aware Proxy on the load balancer's backend service checks each user's identity; grant the group the IAP-secured Web App User role.

entries.title: Dead-lettered messages that never arrive
entries.summary: Dead-lettering is done by the Pub/Sub service agent, which needs Publisher on the dead-letter topic and Subscriber on the source subscription.

entries.title: Self-service projects only in one folder and in the EU
entries.summary: Grant Project Creator on the folder, and set the resource locations constraint on the same folder; both are inherited by the projects created there and affect nobody else.

entries.title: Cloud Build deploying to Cloud Run in another project
entries.summary: A deployer needs a Cloud Run role in the target project and Service Account User (actAs) on the runtime service account it deploys the service to run as.

entries.title: A VM whose service account has the role but still gets a 403
entries.summary: Access scopes limit what a VM's service account tokens can do. Google recommends the cloud-platform scope with IAM roles; changing scopes needs the VM to be stopped.

entries.title: Application log files that never reach Cloud Logging
entries.summary: The Ops Agent collects custom log files through a files receiver, and it writes as the VM's service account, which needs Logs Writer.

entries.title: Recovering overwritten objects for 30 days only
entries.summary: Object Versioning keeps noncurrent versions of overwritten and deleted objects; a lifecycle rule on days since noncurrent removes them after 30 days.

entries.title: A peered VPC sharing the hub's VPN to on-premises
entries.summary: Peered VPCs can use a hub's hybrid connection when the hub exports custom routes and the spoke imports them, and the hub's Cloud Router advertises the spoke's ranges to on-premises.

entries.title: Testing a Cloud Run revision before customers see it
entries.summary: Deploy with --no-traffic and a revision tag: the tag gets its own URL for testing, then traffic is moved to the revision in steps.

entries.title: Pub/Sub events into BigQuery with no pipeline code
entries.summary: A BigQuery subscription writes each Pub/Sub message straight into a table, with no Dataflow job or code; the Pub/Sub service agent needs write access to the table.

entries.title: Monthly OS patching with a compliance report
entries.summary: VM Manager's patch deployments apply OS patches on a schedule, and its patch compliance reporting shows which VMs are missing patches.

entries.title: Cutting egress cost for users in one country
entries.summary: Standard Tier egress costs less but works only with regional resources: a regional external load balancer and a regional Standard Tier address.

entries.title: Private web servers that cannot install updates
entries.summary: Private VMs behind a load balancer still need Cloud NAT for outbound internet access; the load balancer carries inbound requests only and Private Google Access reaches Google APIs only.

entries.title: A GKE cluster in a service project that cannot use the host's ranges
entries.summary: A GKE cluster in a Shared VPC service project needs the service project's GKE service agent to hold Host Service Agent User on the host project and Network User on the subnet.

entries.title: On-premises servers reaching Cloud Storage over HA VPN
entries.summary: On-premises hosts reach Google APIs privately when Cloud Router advertises the private.googleapis.com range over BGP and on-premises DNS resolves the API names to it.

entries.title: Analysts can read the dataset but cannot query it
entries.summary: Reading a dataset and running a query are separate grants: queries are jobs, and jobs need BigQuery Job User on a project.

entries.title: A first regional GKE cluster in a fresh project
entries.summary: A new project needs the service's API enabled, and a regional cluster multiplies nodes by its zones, which can exceed a regional CPU quota.

entries.title: A pipeline creating projects in a standalone organization
entries.summary: A service account cannot be an Organization Owner, but an Organization Administrator can grant it Project Creator on the organization.

entries.title: Every gcloud command as the deploy account
entries.summary: The auth/impersonate_service_account property makes every gcloud command run with short-lived credentials of a service account.

entries.title: A first GPU VM on a Free Trial account
entries.summary: A Free Trial billing account cannot add GPUs or request quota; it must be upgraded to a Paid account before GPU quota can be requested.

entries.title: Anyone in the company can open a billing account
entries.summary: A new organization grants Billing Account Creator to the whole domain; restricting it means granting the role to chosen principals and removing the domain-wide binding.

entries.title: Firewall administrators for every network host project
entries.summary: A role granted on a folder is inherited by present and future projects in it; firewall rules need Compute Security Admin, not Network Admin.

entries.title: A bucket readable by one group, through IAM alone
entries.summary: Uniform bucket-level access turns off ACLs so that only IAM grants access; a bucket-level role then gives one group read access.
